Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a smooth, judder-free feel that suits Elite's flight model; medium textures and shadows look excellent in the cockpit without stressing the shared memory pool. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for most sessions.

profiles.Summary: Elite Dangerous runs on the Steam Deck at a playable level (Verified: Playable), with the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeding the minimum GTX 470 spec and roughly matching the recommended GTX 770/R9 280X class, making 40 fps at medium settings achievable. The game requires an internet connection for most content and has partial controller support, so some UI interactions may need touch or the trackpad.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs versus Deck GPU capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, comfortably above the recommended R9 280X). On first run, check frame rate during a busy station approach or planetary landing — these are the most GPU-intensive scenarios — and drop to the Optimal or MaxBattery profile if the frame rate is unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 upscaled via FSR to keep the GPU well within the 7 W TDP envelope; space flight is smooth at 30 fps and the low preset still looks sharp in cockpit. In-game option names follow the standard Elite Dangerous graphical settings menu — adjust in Options > Graphics.

KnownIssues: Partial controller support means some menus and UI elements may require touch input or trackpad navigation
Always-online requirement means session drops or server issues can interrupt play regardless of settings
Some users report needing Proton Experimental or GE-Proton to avoid launcher/login issues
VR-related assets may cause longer initial load times; the game has a large shader compilation step on first launch

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution at high settings pushes the Deck hard; open space and quiet stations will hit 60 fps, but busy stations or planetary surfaces may dip to 45. Keep Supersampling off — it tanks performance with minimal visual gain on the 800p screen.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap delivers perfectly smooth, low-latency gameplay that suits the deliberate pace of space combat and exploration. Medium textures and shadows keep the galaxy looking good while the GPU stays within the 10 W TDP envelope.

profiles.Summary: Elite Dangerous runs on the Steam Deck at a playable level, benefiting from its relatively modest PC requirements and space-sim gameplay that doesn't demand constant high frame rates. With tuned settings it can hold 40–60 fps in most scenarios, though busy stations and planetary surfaces may cause dips.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 470–770 class, which the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably meets) and the Deck hardware profile. On first run, check frame rate inside a busy station or on a planet surface — those are the most GPU-intensive scenarios — and drop to the Optimal profile if you see sustained dips below 35 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native resolution with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU well under budget; the 30 fps cap and 7 W TDP limit dramatically extend battery life for long exploration sessions. Space flight and supercruise will be smooth; busy stations may dip briefly to 25 fps.

KnownIssues: Requires an online connection and account login at startup, which can cause issues if the Deck's network is slow or unavailable
Partial controller support means some UI menus may require touchscreen or mouse input via the trackpad
Proton compatibility is rated gold/playable — occasional launcher or authentication issues have been reported
Planetary surface and station interiors can cause frame rate drops due to higher geometry and NPC density

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution at uncapped 60 fps is achievable in open space and supercruise, but busy stations or planet surfaces may drop to the mid-40s; consider capping at 55 fps for smoother pacing. Battery life will be short, so docked or USB-C powered play is recommended for extended sessions.
